open_points.subject: M03 Room merging and splitting
open_points.text: When the planner needs it, the candidate is a room status after M05's pattern — `merged` (or superseded) with a reference to the room that replaces it, lists showing current rooms — as a new decision on R0-10. Does not block State 2.
open_points.question: Does Room permanently have no status and no merge/split lifecycle, or must it have a final merged/superseded status, a replacement-room reference, and current-room filtering?
options: Rooms remain immutable forever; merging is represented only by adding another room while all old rooms remain current.
A room can become `merged` or `superseded`, names its replacement, and is excluded from current-room lists.
Merging and splitting use some other lifecycle and relationship model.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the first-release model immutable with no Room status or replacement reference until a new State 0 decision explicitly adds them.

witness.initial: A project has rooms A and B.
events: The planner combines A and B and adds room C for the combined space.
A caller lists the project's current rooms.
outcomes: The list contains A, B and C because old rooms remain ordinary current rooms.
A and B are marked merged or superseded by C, and the current-room list contains only C.
witness.observer: The planner, agent, and every downstream service that lists rooms

open_points.subject: M03 Room import creator
open_points.text: Registry's own record, written by the owner or by Kernel for the agent.
open_points.question: Who creates or writes a Room record brought in by the migration import: the import/migration closure, the owner who confirms the import, or one of the two writers named here?
options: The migration closure creates the imported Room from the legacy record.
The owner is treated as the writer because the owner confirms the import.
The sentence applies only to post-import room creation, and imported Rooms have no writer attribution.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the migration closure as the creating mechanism, from the legacy room record, while storing no creator fact.

witness.initial: Production Registry has no rooms and the accepted migration file contains a room.
events: The owner confirms the one-time import.
Registry installs the imported room under its kept id and name.
outcomes: The Room is classified as written by the import/migration closure.
The Room is classified as written by the owner, or has no writer because neither named writer performed an add-room action.
witness.observer: The contract and model-closure authors deciding which product action creates the Room

open_points.subject: M03 imported Room added instant
open_points.text: written once: the instant it was added and the request id of its create, as the caller gave it (R0-36; owner, 2026-10-31, State 2 A01), absent for a room the import brought in.
open_points.question: For an imported Room, is only the create request id absent, or are both the added instant and the request id absent; if the instant exists, is it copied from the source or minted at import?
options: Only the request id is absent; the source's added instant is copied.
Both the added instant and request id are absent.
The request id is absent and Registry records the import instant as the added instant.
open_points.default_guess: Copy the source's added instant when present and omit only the request id.

witness.initial: The migration file contains a legacy room and an original added timestamp.
events: A later room read or model serialization includes the Room's creation facts.
outcomes: The original added instant is returned and only the request id is absent.
No added instant is returned, or the import instant is returned instead.
witness.observer: The owner or a service reading the imported Room

open_points.subject: M05 ArtifactPointer owner service
open_points.text: its type, one of the vocabulary the specification declared when it was published — or, imported, when the import accepted it — and so its owner service, which the vocabulary fixed (R0-33; "Declared vocabularies"); a later release that removes the type leaves it as it is (State 2 A22);
open_points.question: Does each ArtifactPointer carry an immutable owner-service fact fixed at publication/import, or does it carry only its type and derive the owner service from a vocabulary that may later remove or change that type?
options: Store both the type and the immutable owner service on every pointer.
Store only the type and resolve its owner service from the current vocabulary.
Store the type and retain a versioned vocabulary reference from which its historical owner service is resolved.
open_points.default_guess: Store the immutable owner service beside the type so removed vocabulary entries do not make historical pointers incomplete.

witness.initial: The specification declares artifact type `estimate` with owner service PresuPro.
events: A later release removes that artifact type.
A caller reads the historical pointer.
outcomes: The pointer still directly carries PresuPro as its owner service.
The pointer carries only `estimate`, and its owner service is unavailable unless removed vocabulary data is retained separately.
witness.observer: The owner or service reading artifact history
